name: Montgomery, auction and commission house
trade: auction and commission house, selling merchandize and real estate

proprietors.name: Montgomery
proprietors.basis: The register holds this printed name as person_montgomery with action 'new_resident': the town does not carry a card for them under an id this record can name, so the reading is the name and not yet a person. Dated by the printing window, which bounds the reading and does not date the partnership.

staff.name: Erastus Cobb
staff.basis: The staffing model puts 1 of this role in an auction and commission room at the typical band and 1 at the high end, on directory_1839. A sale is cried by the auctioneer and booked by somebody. 9 auctioneers in 1839. This person is a reconstructed resident of the trade with no workplace of their own; the house is one the business layer already holds, and this row points at it rather than raising anything. shortfall.statement: The staffing model puts 1 hand(s) about this kind of house at its typical band and this house carries 2. It is at its band.
shortfall.counted_here: the reconstructed hands this overlay seats. A hand a SOURCE names carries its own citation in staff[] and is counted by the attested join, not by this.
shortfall.replaceable_by: a source naming a hand at this house, which retires the seat it replaces, or the mint T-1448 ordered, which draws the rest

locations.basis: The paper names a street and no house on it.
locations.limit_reason: The paper names South Water Street and nothing narrower; the anchor is a reach of south_water and names nothing narrower.

dates.basis: No opening is announced. The first printing, 1835-06-24, is the bound: the house was trading by then and the record does not say when it began.

proprietor_community.basis: This record names nobody the resident layer holds a card for, so there is no person to read a community off. The silence is in the register.

replaceable_by: A directory, a deed or a later reading that names this house's premises, its staff or its dates more exactly than the newspapers do.
